title: Execution Environment and Toolchain Checklist (Field Experience)
description: Kali container, per-task isolated tmp directories, base64 code transfer, and labeling results as local/remote
detail:
Field configuration from TPT-Agent (19th place in a past exercise):
1. Core tooling uses only two primitives: execute Python code + execute commands (fewer tools can better unlock model potential)
2. Use an independent tmp directory per task to prevent contamination; run commands via docker exec and pass code into the sandbox via base64 to avoid escaping trial-and-error
3. Label every execution result as "this is a local sandbox result" to prevent misinterpreting it as remote
4. Add timeouts and output truncation to command execution
5. Knowledge base: retrieve precise keywords from hacktricks/PayloadsAllTheThings/HowToHunt and take the top N results; the CVE library supports product name + version lookup
6. Lesson learned: libc/architecture incompatibilities can break preinstalled toolsets — test tool compatibility on the target CVM before the engagement
Source: https://github.com/CloudEver-Team/tencent_pentration_tool + enoch.host retrospective
